name: hdi-substrate-from-csv
prompt: model this substrate from the csv

inputs.notes: A synthetic Quillmere Circuit Works stackup report (fictional fabricator, fictional laminate, soldermask and foil products): 12-layer HDI, 2+8+2 sequential build-up, two dielectric rows (D-BU, D-PP) that differ only in Dk, a 6-via inventory (4 laser microvias, 2 drilled from each side; 1 buried; 1 unfilled through via tented on the top only), 4 controlled impedance targets each quoted on coated microstrip and asymmetric stripline, a DIFF-90-UNC uncoupled region, an uncontrolled STANDARD row, 19 mappable fab rules (two drill minimums, laser and mechanical) plus 5 capability limits, and an inclusive-limits note. It shares the JS1 kit report's SECTION layout and no value a substrate carries, so a copied kit board fails it.

runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
expected_output: A single-file substrate (board.py) in which every value traces to a report row: an explicit 12-layer Stackup of 25 entries (not Symmetric, since the report names both halves) whose sum reconciles with the 1.402 mm finished and 1.432 mm overall totals; one material class per material row, with D-BU (Dk 3.30) and D-PP (Dk 3.38) kept apart and each dielectric's material_name carrying its Product; finished copper thickness and matte-side Rz in mm; exactly the 6 offered vias, the bottom-side microvias UV-3 and UV-4 coded from L12 and L11, and TH-1 unfilled and tented on the top only; the 19 mappable fab rules with min_drill_diameter holding the 0.075 mm laser minimum and the 0.150 mm mechanical minimum hand-checked; SE-50, SE-42, SE-60 and DIFF-90 on both geometries with velocity from Eps_eff, neck-downs only where the report quotes them (none on SE-60), DIFF-90-UNC as the pair's uncoupled region, and reference planes from Ref_layers at 3x their own dielectric height (0.240 mm to the build-up side, 0.381 mm to the core side of L3 and L10); STANDARD documented but not modelled; and the SKILL.md Substrate completeness check block filled in the completion summary.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package

the substrate in board.py matches the report row for row: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction, fab rules, routing structures with uncoupled regions and reference planes, and no structure for the uncontrolled row (the grader reads every expected value from the CSV)

no invented numbers: every value in board.py that no report row backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows

future_cases: No micro cases until a run of this case shows a failure the grader cannot see. Later artifact cases planned: the same kind of stackup from a PDF fab report (no CSV structure to lean on), and a smaller JLCPCB predefined-path case.
